ch34.note: Liao Yaoxiang (廖耀湘, 1906–1968), a Nationalist general whose crack New Sixth Army had fought in the Burma campaign; his army was destroyed and he himself captured in the Communists' Liao-Shen offensive in Manchuria in 1948.

The regional Nationalist command for the Beiping–Tianjin theater in the civil war ('bandit-suppression' meaning the campaign against the Communists), headed by General Fu Zuoyi—the authority under which Chen's special unit operated.

The building had been the seat of the Provisional Executive Government, the short-lived Beijing regime of 1924–26 over which the warlord Duan Qirui presided as 'provisional chief executive' after the elected republic collapsed.
The proverb zuo chi shan kong (坐吃山空), 'sit idle and eat, and a whole mountain is emptied out'—to live on savings with nothing coming in exhausts any fortune, however large.

Tan Family Cooking (谭家菜, Tanjiacai), a celebrated Beijing haute cuisine that began in the private household kitchen of the late-Qing official Tan Zongjun and grew famous enough to outlast him—a byword for refined banqueting.

Tang Lusun (唐鲁孙, 1908–1985), of Manchu banner descent, a much-loved essayist on Chinese food and the vanished customs of old Beijing, who wrote prolifically after his move to Taiwan—hence Chen cites him as an authority on such things.
